name: RAG - Automated Document Ingestion

nodes.name: Watch Folder / Bucket
nodes.notes: Fires when a new file is added to the shared 'knowledge-base' Drive folder (swap for S3 Trigger / Local Folder Trigger as needed).

nodes.name: Classify Department & Sensitivity
nodes.notes: Lightweight rules engine (folder path + filename keywords, e.g. '/finance/' -> department=finance, 'confidential' in name -> access_level=confidential) that tags each incoming file before ingestion. Falls back to department=general, access_level=internal.

nodes.name: POST to Flask Ingestion Webhook
nodes.notes: Calls the Flask microservice (app_flask_ingest.py) which chunks, embeds, and writes the file into ChromaDB with RBAC metadata.

nodes.name: Notify #rag-ingestion (Slack)
nodes.notes: Posts a summary (filename, department, access_level, chunk_count) so the team has visibility into what just entered the knowledge base.

nodes.name: On Failure -> Alert
nodes.notes: Wired to the workflow's error output; posts to #rag-ingestion-alerts and retries once after 60s for transient network errors.

_readme: This is a documentation-oriented export (hand-authored, trimmed of n8n's internal IDs/positions) describing the automated ingestion pipeline referenced in the resume: 'agentic AI workflow automation system using n8n microservice pipelines... automated document ingestion, ETL-style data preprocessing, and ~40% reduction in query response latency.' The 40% latency reduction comes from decoupling ingestion (async, batched, off the hot path) from the synchronous query API — see README.md 'Why two services' section.
